Based on the search results, here's what's happening with Node.js LTS versions in October 2026:

Node.js 26 is scheduled to transition to LTS in October 2026, making it the current LTS version at that time. Node.js 26 becomes the long-lived target once it enters LTS in October.

Additionally, as of October 2026, all future Node releases will be LTS releases, marking a significant change to Node.js's release strategy. Starting with Node.js 27, the project moves to one major release a year: a single Current release each April, promoted to Long-Term Support (LTS) each October, with every release now becoming LTS and the odd/even split retired.

So in October 2026, **Node.js 26 becomes the LTS version**, and from that point forward, the entire release model changes to make every Node.js release an LTS release.
